extracted.intended_audience: NIH R01 applicants, grant writers, and institutional grant administrators (UCSF researchers preparing biosketches and budget justifications)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing NIH-format biographical sketches, research support entries, and detailed budget justification (personnel, supplies, travel, equipment, recharge rates, QA/assay validation) for an R01 renewal application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Name, eRA Commons user name (credential), Position Title. Follow the five-page limit strictly for the NIH biographical sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Institution and location, Degree (if applicable), Completion Date (MM/YYYY), and Field of Study. Arrange entries beginning with baccalaureate and include postdoctoral/residency where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support entries (ongoing & completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support — list ongoing and completed research support with grant number, dates, agency, title, description of aims and role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry should include project/grant identifier (e.g., R01 AI098472), funding agency (NIH/NIAID), project title, project dates, a brief description of the study goals/aims, and the individual's Role (e.g., Role: Co-Investigator, Role: Collaborator, Role: Principal Investigator). Examples on the page illustrate how to present ongoing and completed support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel: name, position, effort, and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget justification personnel entries list personnel (name and title), calendar months of effort per year (e.g., 1.2 calendar months years 1-3; 1.8 calendar months years 4-5), and a narrative of responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each listed person (PI, co-investigators, staff), provide the percent/caledar months of effort by project year and describe specific responsibilities and contributions to the project (e.g., oversight of hair collection, assay validation, data analysis, mentoring). Examples: Monica Gandhi (PI) with specified calendar months and oversight duties; Dr. Gerona as principal analytic chemist with assay development/validation duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary Cap disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Current annual institutional salary exceeds the current Federal Executive Level II Salary Cap of $185,100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When institutional salaries exceed the federal Executive Level II cap, explicitly note this in the budget justification. This disclosure flags that requested salary amounts may be above the federal limit and should be accounted for accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefit rates and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe Benefit Rates: UCSF’s Office of Research published fringe benefit rates: Benefit Rate 07/01/16-06/30/17 / 07/01/17-06/30/18 / 07/01/18-06/30/19, with Academic Benefits and Staff Benefits percentages (e.g., 33.90% / 41.90% etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution-published fringe benefit rates with effective date ranges and separate rates for academic vs. staff benefits. Include citation to the institutional source (Office of Research) so reviewers can verify rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget projections follow institutional policy and prorating
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to University of California policy, the salaries in the initial budget are based on current published UC salary scales and include University mandated range adjustments and merit increases scheduled to occur before the proposed project start date. Projections for salaries, fringe benefits, and merit increases have been prorated to conform to the grant years of this proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets must use current institutional salary scales, include planned merit increases at scheduled times, and prorate those increases across the grant period. Explain assumptions and that projections conform to institutional policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and supplies justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Itemize and justify materials and supplies (computers, software, printers, hair collection supplies, laboratory supplies for assay validation and sample analysis) with estimated costs and linkage to study activities (e.g., number of samples, years when collection occurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific items, their purpose in the project (e.g., validation, sample processing, analysis), estimated costs by year, and tie quantities/costs to the workload (e.g., ~8000 hair samples). Include consumables needed for LC-MS/MS and sample processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel justification (international and domestic)
rubrics_metrics.description: International trips: list destinations (Uganda, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe), purpose (overseeing sample collection, technology transfer, attendance at retreats), duration (e.g., 10 days), and estimated costs; Domestic trips: list conferences and purposes for presenting findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget travel by trip with purpose, destinations, duration, and estimated per-trip cost (airfare, lodging, meals, local transportation, registration). Specify years when trips will occur and total per-year travel budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and specimen shipping costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication: budget publication costs per year (years 2-4 and year 5). Specimen shipping: estimate costs per year for shipping specimens back to UCSF during study years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide yearly estimates for publication fees and specimen shipping, identify which years incur costs, and give total projected costs over the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment lease and service agreements must be costed and apportioned
rubrics_metrics.description: LC-MS/MS Equipment Lease and LC/MS-MS Service Agreement costs should be shown with total and apportioned per year based on the time the equipment will be used for the aims (e.g., Year 1 validation; Years 2 and 3 heavy use; Years 4 and 5 diminished use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show lease and service costs, and explicitly apportion costs across project years in proportion to equipment usage by aims. This demonstrates fair allocation of capital/service expenses to the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & Network recharge and CCDSS justification, regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Per review and agreement by our cognizant federal agency, UCSF data network costs are an allowable direct expense. Provide per capita recharge rates (e.g., $/month/FTE for given date ranges) and describe Computing and Communication Device Support Services (CCDSS). Reference applicable OMB requirements, including 2 CFR Part 220 (formerly Circular A-21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include institutional recharge rates with effective dates, a brief description of services covered, a statement that costs are allowable per cognizant agency review, and citation to OMB/regulatory guidance. Provide contact direction for DCA questions (Division of Cost Allocation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay validation and CPQA submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation of hair assays and submission of analytic validation reports/standard operating procedures (AVR/SOP) to CPQA for peer review and approval prior to sample analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that assays must be validated and AVR/SOPs submitted to the DAIDS Clinical Pharmacology Quality Assurance (CPQA) program for peer review/approval before analyzing study samples. Note which assays have already been approved where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance and QA monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Director monitors and inspects analytical studies to assure that equipment, personnel, methods, practices, records, and controls are in conformance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe QA duties: monitoring equipment, personnel competence, method conformance, reviewing records, recognizing irregularities and invalid results, and ensuring GLP compliance across assay validation and sample analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen collection/processing/storage and regulatory oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure collection, transfer, processing, and storage of specimens follow proper QC monitored procedures; set up specimen tracking system for movement and storage; oversee IRB and national requirements and the process for specimen shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate in-country QA coordinators (e.g., Uganda-based) to coordinate local specimen handling, enforce QC procedures, maintain specimen tracking, ensure compliance with IRB/national regulations, and manage shipment logistics and material transfer agreements.
